name: Turkish-Style Vegan Tofu Scramble (Vegan Menemen)

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
finely diced shishito, padrón, or Chinese green long peppers

instructions.primary_message: In a medium nonstick or cast iron skillet, heat olive oil over low heat until barely warm. Add Urfa chilies, oregano (if using), onion, and peppers. Season with salt and a very generous amount of black pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until very soft, about 8 minutes. Add tomatoes and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until deepened in color, about 5 minutes longer. Remove half of mixture and reserve.

Add tofu and season with salt and pepper. Cook, folding gently, until tofu is heated through and broken into large curds. Gently fold in reserved vegetable mixture. Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with bread.

schema_metadata.keywords: breakfast, easy, Istanbul, menemen, quick, tofu, turkish

description: Menemen—eggs scrambled with olive oil, onions, chilies, and tomatoes—is traditionally made by slow-cooking onions and hot chilies in olive oil, then seasoning them with dried chilies and oregano and stewing them with tomatoes. The eggs go in at the last moment and are cooked until just barely set. With so many strong flavors and a texture easily captured by silken tofu, it works great as a vegan breakfast.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano (optional); Chopped fresh parsley, to garnish; Bread, for serving

Optional substitutions: chopped peeled ripe fresh tomatoes → drained canned tomatoes

Notes: Urfa chilies are smoky chilies from Turkey. They can be ordered online. If unavailable, substitute regular or smoked paprika.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
